algorithm: Extension-to-folder mapping with a plan-then-execute move pass

classes.desc: Sorts the top-level files of a folder into subfolders by extension.
classes.name: FileOrganizer

data_flow_ascii:
seeded sample files -> demo_workspace/ (flat)
FileOrganizer.plan -> [(source, dest)] by extension map
FileOrganizer.execute -> shutil.move -> categorized subfolders
before/after trees printed to stdout
description_sentence: A file organizer that generates sample files, plans moves by extension mapping, and sorts them into categorized subfolders.
failure_note: Unknown extensions go to a 'misc' folder instead of erroring; --dry-run prints the plan without moving anything.

functions.desc: Folder name for a file's extension, or 'misc' when unknown.
functions.name: FileOrganizer.category_for

functions.desc: [(source, destination), ...] for every top-level file in root.
functions.name: FileOrganizer.plan

functions.desc: Carry out a plan from plan(); return the moves that happened.
functions.name: FileOrganizer.execute

functions.desc: Create n seeded sample files directly inside root; return their names.
functions.name: make_sample_files
functions.signature: make_sample_files(root: str, n: int, rng: random.Random) -> list

functions.desc: Relative paths of everything under root, directories first, sorted.
functions.name: list_tree

functions.desc: Generate sample files, show before/after, then organize them.
functions.name: run_demo
functions.signature: run_demo(seed: int, n_files: int, dry_run: bool) -> int

functions.desc: Build the command-line parser for the demo.
functions.name: build_parser

functions.desc: Parse flags and run the organizer demo.
functions.name: main

label: file organizer
output_shape: Prints before/after directory trees of demo_workspace plus the move plan and moved-file count.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that tidies a messy folder into categorized subfolders, showing you the plan before it moves anything.

qa.a: The extension map comes from @@TOPIC_PARAMS@@; any extension not listed is routed to a 'misc' folder.
qa.q: How does it decide which folder a file goes to?

qa.a: plan() computes every move first, so --dry-run can show the full plan and execute() just carries it out.
qa.q: What is the point of plan() versus execute()?

qa.a: Yes: the demo wipes and recreates ./demo_workspace at startup, so reruns are clean and deterministic.
qa.q: Is the demo safe to rerun?

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python that sorts files into extension-mapped folders with a plan-then-execute pass and dry-run mode.
run_notes: --files sets the sample count; --dry-run prints the move plan without moving anything. Works inside ./demo_workspace.
scaling_note: Single-machine, single-threaded moves; fine for thousands of files, not a distributed file pipeline.
storage_note: Only the demo_workspace folder it creates at runtime; no state is kept between runs beyond those files.
tradeoff_note: Top-level files only keeps the logic predictable; recursive organizing would risk surprising moves in nested folders.
